% PRELIMINARY: single-run numbers from results/replay/. Regenerated by
% paper/make_replay_tex.py once results/replay3/ (three seeds) is complete.
\newcommand{\ReplayAbstract}{On a real cluster it resizes pods in place without restarts and reacts to a flash crowd sooner than the HPA, but a single-run comparison does not establish an advantage at matched cost.}
\newcommand{\ReplayBody}{An open-loop load generator replayed a 24-minute demand trace (12 minutes of an Azure trace, then a flash crowd to five times the mean) against a CPU-bound service costing 61\,ms of CPU per request, with a 0.3\,s latency objective. In one run per controller, CHIMERA on a request-rate signal had 28.6\,\% violations at 81.8 core-minutes, against 35.5\,\% at 77.1 for the HPA at a 50\,\% target and 51.1\,\% at 72.8 at a 70\,\% target. With one run and two HPA points there is neither a frontier nor a sample, and we do not claim an equal-cost win. Every controller missed the objective far more often than in simulation: a 61\,ms request on a pod limited to half a core exceeds a single CFS quota period.}
\newcommand{\ReplayConclusion}{On a real cluster the operator works and reacts faster than the HPA to a flash crowd, but a single live run does not establish a cost-matched advantage; a larger live study is the main work that remains.}
